official.title: Research Assistant
official.description_text:
Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 16 000 students and 5 200 employees, including 446 professors. Our campus is in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland.  Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.
We are now looking for a
Research Assistant
at Aalto University School of Business for a project examining how joint versus sole custody affects children’s and parents’ long-term outcomes, including education, health and employment. The applicant must be enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree programme. We hope the selected candidate can start as soon as possible, or by 11.1.2027 the latest.
Your role
The main role is to help build a unique research dataset by collecting information on custody decisions from Finnish district courts. This will involve, for example:
contacting courts
coordinating access and data collection arrangements
systematically extracting and recording information from court documents.
To succeed in this role, you will need
A proactive, independent approach, with the confidence to take ownership of communication with courts and follow requests through to completion.
Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and sound judgment when handling confidential information.
An interest in empirical research in economics or a related social science.
Strong capability and positive attitude toward data processing and analysis.
Excellent Finnish and English language skills, both written and spoken, is required.
Bachelor’s or Master’s level studies in a relevant field.
What we offer
Opportunity to participate in research
as part of a vibrant international community: You will work within a community of students, researchers, and other professionals advancing societally significant goals in science and education.
Support, coaching and sparring
when you feel you need it.
Great possibilities for
competence development and learning
. This is an excellent opportunity for a student considering a PhD to gain hands-on experience in an ambitious research project and work closely with the research team. Depending on your interests and the project’s progress, the work could also provide a foundation for a master’s thesis or your own future research.
Meaningful and inspiring environment
. We are proud of our purpose to shape a sustainable future. We renew society with research-based knowledge, creativity and an entrepreneurial mindset.
A culture where everyone is valued.
Our work is guided by the values of Aalto University: responsibility, courage, and collaboration. We want to be an open community where equality and inclusion enable curiosity, innovation, collaboration and wellbeing.
We aim to combine the best of remote and on-site work and offer flexible working hours. Your on-site workplace is located on the Otaniemi campus, with diverse services and excellent transport connections. The position is part-time with 20-40 % working time percentage and fixed term for approximately 3-6 months. The salary is determined according to the university salary system used at Aalto University. The salary level is approximately 2 377,68 €/month - 2 488,27 €/month (100 % working time, the salary is determined by the part-time percentage).
Join us!
To apply, please share your CV, motivation letter and transcript of records with us through our recruitment site ("Apply now!”) latest at 23.59pm (EET) 22nd of November 2026.
Please note: Aalto University’s employees should apply for the position via our internal HR system Workday (Internal Jobs) by using their existing Workday user account (not via the external webpage for open positions). If you are a student or visitor at Aalto University, please apply with your personal email address (not aalto.fi) via
Aalto University open positions
Documents to include with the application (as a single PDF file)
Motivation letter
CV
Transcript of records
For more information about the role, please contact Kristiina Huttunen (kristiina.huttunen(at)aalto.fi. For questions related to the application process, please contact HR Advisor Saskia Raatikainen, hr-biz(at)aalto.fi.
We will go through applications, and we may invite suitable candidates to interview already during the application period. We aim to have a transparent and equal recruitment process, so feel free to ask us for feedback.

ai.summary: Research assistant role at Aalto University School of Business collecting court data on custody decisions for a longitudinal outcomes study. Position requires systematic data extraction, court coordination, and strong Finnish/English language skills. Work is administrative and social-science focused, not technical or XR-related.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic alignment. The position concerns family economics, custody law, and social outcomes—entirely outside the researcher's domain of human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, and wayfinding. The mention of 'research' is generic administrative support in a different discipline.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological overlap. The role involves data collection logistics (court contact, document extraction, confidentiality handling) and quantitative social science. While the researcher has user-study and quantitative-research experience, the operational context (legal document processing, Finnish court systems) shares no methods with immersive systems design, user evaluation in VR, or spatial cognition research.

growth_value.rationale: Negligible growth for the target identity. The researcher would not develop capabilities in human-centred XR, immersive systems, spatial learning, or collaborative design. Administrative data collection provides no pathway to doctoral research in HCI or immersive systems. The researcher's timeline (MSc thesis stage) suggests a doctoral track, not a detour into social science administration.

strategic_value.rationale: Aalto is a respected institution and European location meets geography constraints. However, this specific role (School of Business, custody research) offers no supervision, mentorship, or network value for an HCI/XR researcher. Part-time (20–40%), fixed-term (3–6 months) contract does not build towards a doctoral position or research independence in the target domain.

eligibility_flags: Requires fluent Finnish (written and spoken); researcher profile does not list Finnish language proficiency.
Position requires bachelor's or master's student enrolment; researcher is enrolled MSc but in a different institution and discipline.
Fixed-term 3–6 month role ends ~May 2027; researcher's thesis timeline unclear—potential conflict if MSc completion is imminent.
risks: Complete domain mismatch (family economics ≠ immersive HCI) delays or derails doctoral preparation.
Part-time administrative role offers no research mentorship, publication opportunities, or professional network in HCI/XR.
No pathway to doctoral candidacy; role is terminal administrative contract.
Opportunity cost: 3–6 months could be spent finalizing MSc thesis, publishing, or pursuing aligned postgraduate positions.

eligibility_reasons: funding/salary not confirmed on the posting
whether a completed degree is required before employment is not stated; your MSc is still in progress — verify with the source
